column1: Reporting to: Ramesh sir (CTO) and Kavitha mam (Tech Lead)
Reporting period: 24 August–25 October 2026 | Updated: 21 October 2026

column2:
• Met Ramesh sir and Kavitha mam on 27 August.
• Discussed practical ML problems, factory automation challenges, and possible project directions.
column3: • Needed to finalise a suitable, high-impact problem statement.

column2:
• Reviewed the existing VisureX approach and project poster.
• Researched operator logbook digitization for MSMEs.
• Drafted and submitted initial proposal on 2 September: Hands-free logbook & production tracking using Meta Glasses, ArUco marker gaze locks, mobile edge proxy, and CV dial/tray reading.
column3:
• Changes in ambient factory lighting and camera orientation affected reading stability.
• Wearable hardware constraints and edge processing reliability raised feasibility questions.

column2:
• Explored Meta glasses workflow feasibility vs. fixed industrial inspection.
• Researched optical capture bounds, Bluetooth bandwidth limits, and display parsing models.
• Coordinated technical review on MSME shop-floor ergonomics and deployment costs.
column3:
• Capture latency and battery constraints in harsh industrial settings.
• Need to evaluate whether wearable glasses or fixed-surface visual inspection provides higher industry demand.

column2:
• Pivoted project scope toward automated flat surface quality inspection.
• Submitted revised project abstract on 15 September: Integrated visual inspection platform combining 2D surface anomaly detection with Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) for solar panels and sheet materials.
• Defined the dual-engine concept: classical CV for preprocessing and ML for defect segmentation.
column3:
• Narrowing down specific anomaly classes and defining quantifiable severity criteria.
• Limited public availability of pixel-level defect masks.

column2:
• Conducted literature review on solar photovoltaic (PV) soiling and defect inspection.
• Formulated project boundary: in-scope stains (dust/soiling, bird droppings, mud) vs. out-of-scope defects (snow, mechanical cracks, electrical burns).
• Prepared initial architectural proposal comparing single-stage classifiers against two-stage segmentation.
column3:
• Scheduled review meeting was postponed due to team travel.
• Most public datasets only provide image-level labels rather than pixel-level segmentation masks.

column2:
• Attended technical review on 28 September with Ramesh sir and Kavitha mam.
• Finalized the two-stage inspection architecture: Stage A for panel localization/rectification and Stage B for stain segmentation.
• Defined explainability goals: replacing black-box classification with exact stain coverage % and localized hotspot alerts.
column3:
• Background artifacts (sky, roof tiles, shadows) distort coverage metrics if panels are not strictly rectified.
• Need for a robust boundary-detection baseline.

column2:
• Attended meeting at WCTE Centre on 7 October discussing plausible datasets for model training.
• Evaluated public repositories: Kaggle (Faulty Solar Panel Images), Mendeley Data (Solar Panel Soiling), and Roboflow Universe.
• Designed data-hygiene protocol: Perceptual Hashing (pHash) to detect duplicate web images and prevent train–test leakage.
column3:
• Reused images across public repositories cause severe train–test data leakage.
• Extreme class imbalance between large clean areas and small, high-risk bird droppings.

column2:
• Set up local development environment (Python 3.12, PyTorch, Albumentations, SMP, OpenCV).
• Finalized operational decision rules: High Stain if Coverage ≥ 10% or any single bird blob ≥ 2%; 4×4 sub-panel grid breakdown.
• Implemented Stage A perspective homography rectifier to canonical 512×512 view.
• Formulated dataset curation pipeline: pHash deduplication, 70/15/15 group-stratified splits, and SAM 2/CVAT-aligned ground-truth mask preparation.
column3:
• Ensuring augmentations avoid hue shifts that misrepresent dust tones.
• Adapting models and training pipelines for efficient CPU execution.

column2:
• Ingested and standardized multi-source datasets (Kaggle, Mendeley, Roboflow) into unified manifest.
• Model is currently in the training process for the computer vision solar panel stain detection and segmentation network.
• Monitoring training iterations, batch scheduling, and convergence across initial epochs.
column3:
• Training execution time on local workstation hardware.
• Balancing batch size and memory footprint during segmentation training.
